key_insight: Conditional rectified-flow generation paired with exact latent-space refinement enables concurrent design of printable scaffold microstructures and their spatial assignments to meet mechanical targets.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports highly porous bone scaffolds that preserve target structural responses, with potential extension to metal additive manufacturing.
method: Generate periodic lattice cells using a conditional rectified-flow model.
Refine cells in latent space using exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities.
Jointly optimize cell geometries and spatial assignments under mechanical and feature-size constraints.
evidence_signal: In computational benchmarks, all eight rabbit flow-started refinements achieved under 1% error across six target moduli; human femoral scaffolds reached 63% cortical porosity with compliance within 2% and 84% cancellous porosity with strain-energy deviations below 0.25%.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational validation; physical printability, fatigue durability, and biological performance remain to be established experimentally.
paper_title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
